tts_summary:
Good morning. Here's what you need to know heading into Monday September 21st.

Markets are kicking off the week on a surprisingly positive note. S&P futures are up about 65 basis points, Nasdaq is up 110 basis points, and the Russell 2000 is up 47 basis points. Asia was broadly higher — Korea led with gains of 165 basis points, Hang Seng up 118 basis points. Europe is up 85 to 120 basis points with strength in industrials, basic resources, tech, and banks. Treasuries have a bid, with yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve.

Now here's the thing — this rally is confounding because the weekend news was almost entirely negative. Houthis launched a major missile and drone attack on Saudi Arabia. Ukraine hit Russia with its largest drone strike of the war. On the AI side, Anthropic's IPO was delayed, their 2027 revenue projections came in underwhelming, OpenAI disclosed roughly 280 billion dollars in projected negative free cash flow through 2030, and Oracle's data center debt tied to its New Mexico Project Jupiter facility is reportedly hitting a wall with lenders. That's a lot of bad news to rally through.

So what's driving the bid? Two words: UN General Assembly. The event runs this week in New York and brings together leaders from across the Middle East, including Iran. Trump said Sunday he'd be open to meeting with Iran's president. He also reportedly pulled back from authorizing air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday night. Markets are latching onto any hint of diplomatic progress because if oil comes down meaningfully, the macro picture changes fast — lower yields, less hawkish Fed, better margins, improved consumer confidence. That cascade effect is the bull case in a nutshell.

On the Fed front, the market is pricing roughly 33 basis points of hikes over the final two meetings of the year, with about 50-50 odds on October 28th. Fed Presidents Schmid and Kashkari both reminded us last week that inflation is running hot well beyond just energy. Treasury is also leaning heavily on short-term bill issuance — over a trillion dollars in T-bills over the next 12 months, pushing above their own 20 percent target.

On the company side, Disney's parks business is standing out positively — outperforming peers using price promotions to drive attendance while the broader theme park industry slumps. Novo Nordisk is under pressure in Europe after failing to provide granular financial targets at its analyst day — investors wanted numbers and didn't get them. Oracle remains a concern following that Financial Times data center debt piece. And the Paramount-Warner deal faces ongoing regulatory complexity with California settlement talks that may require divesting Comedy Central and preserving CNN's editorial independence — but not all state attorneys general are aligned.

The big events to watch this week beyond today: US-China Trump-Xi summit on Thursday with modest tariff cuts possible, US flash PMIs Wednesday morning, and Meta's Connect conference Wednesday night where Zuckerberg delivers the keynote. The trade truce with China doesn't expire until November 10th, so Sunday's failure to extend it formally isn't a crisis yet — but the direction of tariffs is still headed higher over the coming weeks.

Bottom line: the tape wants to rally on Middle East diplomatic hope, and even a small improvement in Iran tensions would be a big deal for oil and the broader macro. But the fundamental picture is still fragile, and the AI infrastructure complex faces real scrutiny after a damaging weekend of headlines. Stay nimble, watch the oil price, and watch every headline out of the UN General Assembly.
